claims: The northern lights (aurora borealis) are caused by solar particles colliding with Earth’s atmosphere.
Northern lights are best viewed between September and April.
Northern lights are best viewed particularly from 10 P.M. to 2 A.M.
Northern lights appear in high-latitude regions like Norway, Iceland, and Alaska.
Prime viewing locations for northern lights are within the aurora zone (60-75 degrees latitude).
Prime viewing locations for northern lights include Tromso, Norway.
Prime viewing locations for northern lights include Swedish Lapland.
Prime viewing locations for northern lights include Iceland.
Prime viewing locations for northern lights include Alaska.
The peak season for northern lights is late September to late March.
High-activity months for northern lights are typically March, April, September, and October.
The best viewing time of night for northern lights is generally between 11 P.M. and 2 A.M., according to Visit Norway.
The aurora is caused by charged particles from the sun interacting with oxygen and nitrogen in the Earth's magnetic field.
Increased solar activity, known as a solar maximum, produces more intense and frequent aurora displays.
NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center provides 30-minute forecasts.
